identity.industry: Steel Wire & Tyre-Reinforcement Materials — mid-stream wire drawing/coating

summary.oneLiner: A gas-price shock in the first 45 days of the quarter cut blended EBITDA from ~INR 7/kg to INR 2/kg because management chose to absorb the cost rather than reprice 30–40 days of committed orders — a deliberate relationship call, not a structural break. Margins were back to INR 7–8/kg from ~15 May, and the company is holding its 20% volume and 20% EBITDA growth guidance for the remaining three quarters. The real story underneath is the Specialty ramp: first Steel Cord bulk-trial order from a leading Indian tyre maker, IHT running ahead of plan, and B2C already at ~10% of sales in its first full year.

one-line thesis: A gas-price shock in the first 45 days of the quarter cut blended EBITDA from ~INR 7/kg to INR 2/kg because management chose to absorb the cost rather than reprice 30–40 days of committed orders — a deliberate relationship call, not a structural break. Margins were back to INR 7–8/kg from ~15 May, and the company is holding its 20% volume and 20% EBITDA growth guidance for the remaining three quarters. The real story underneath is the Specialty ramp: first Steel Cord bulk-trial order from a leading Indian tyre maker, IHT running ahead of plan, and B2C already at ~10% of sales in its first full year.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 1,168 cr | +25% | Volume 112,000 MT vs 104,000 MT in Q1FY26 |
| EBITDA / margin | INR 57 cr / ~4.9% | sharply down | Blended INR 4–4.5/kg vs INR 6.5–7/kg run-rate; first 45 days at INR 2/kg |
| PAT (rptd) | INR 20 cr | down | Depressed by the same gas/consumable absorption |
| Gross margin | cost-plus model | — | Any RM/consumable move normally passed through; 70–80% of inventory covered by firm-rate orders |
| Order book | 30–40 days of firm-rate orders carried | — | This is the natural hedge — and this quarter it was the problem |
| Cash / net debt | Operating cash flow INR 121 cr in the quarter | +ve | Free cash from operating activities ~INR 120 cr; FY27 CFO target INR 350 cr |
> **Adjustment to call out explicitly:** consumable/gas costs rose ~INR 5,000/tonne blended almost overnight; management did *not* renegotiate the ~30–40 days of already-committed orders. That single decision is the whole margin gap. All new orders booked from 1 April carried the escalated price. Gas cost is still ~1.5x on a blended basis (up to 3x at some plants) — it has not come down, it has simply been passed on.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue/volume growth:** "we are still working towards achieving a growth of 20% for the rest of the year" — 20% volume growth; EBITDA guidance "would also still remain 20%", i.e. at least in line with volume.
- **Margin:** back to INR 7–8/kg blended EBITDA from ~15 May; specialty wires expected at a higher EBITDA than base business. IHT/OHT targeted at INR 10–20/kg once at optimum utilisation.
- **Order book / inflow:** no Steel Cord order book yet — trial stage only. Confirmed order book expected after 3–4 trial stages, each 2–3 months, i.e. 6–8 months out. More trial orders expected from other customers within Q2FY27.
- **Capex / commissioning:** INR 200–250 cr capex for FY27 and "every year" thereafter — deliberately capped. OHT to be commissioned by end of FY27, taking IHT+OHT capacity from 9,000 T to 15,000 T.
- **Returns:** 25% ROCE target in the *current* business "in a very short while", independent of Specialty.
- **Cash:** INR 350 cr operating cash flow target for FY27 (against INR 330 cr delivered in FY26 vs a INR 250 cr target); INR 800 cr combined across FY27+FY28.
order book & pipeline: The company runs on a 30–40 day firm-rate order book rather than a long-cycle backlog, matched against 30–40 days of steel inventory — a deliberate natural hedge that normally passes commodity moves straight to the customer. Steel Cord is the one genuinely new pipeline: the company has cleared sample approval with most customers, and one customer skipped field trial entirely and moved directly to a bulk trial order. Four trial stages remain; each takes about two to three months. Management explicitly refused to name the customer and stressed "there is no order book honestly there" yet.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Core (low + high carbon):** low carbon is 50–55% of volume. No end-segment is more than 25% of sales; no customer more than 3–4%. Segments served: automotive (largest), consumer durables, power & cable, infra, general engineering, agriculture, poultry.
- **Specialty (~35,000 T today):** Steel Cord pilot 20,000 T; IHT 9,000 T; OHT to add 6,000 T. Vision is 2 lakh tonnes of Specialty.
- **B2C:** new range for farming, fencing and poultry launched in the quarter; already ~10% of sales. Q2 and Q3 are seasonally soft for B2C; Q1 and Q4 are stronger.
- **Sanand:** expansion under way with ~90,000 T of wire capex. Earlier talk of selling the facility was corrected — only excess land may be partly sold, not the plant.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Steel Cord import substitution:** 60–65% of the Indian market is served by imports; management targets 45–50% share at the 2 lakh tonne stage. Explicitly *not* an export play — Indian wire rod costs INR 10–15/kg more than Chinese, which is "50% of my margin".
- **IHT/OHT into EV:** both used in automotive, with EV a large part of consumption. 80% of IHT customers have already given approvals; the remaining 20% are at advanced stages. Targeting 50% IHT utilisation in the month following the call and 60–80% by end FY27.
- **B2C brand extension:** ambition is 50% of the low-carbon book through B2C, i.e. ~25% of total sales, at 20–30% higher EBITDA/tonne than B2B.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Backward integration into machinery:** "more than 50% of our equipments we manufacture ourselves." This is the load-bearing advantage — it compresses capex planning from 12–18 months to six months and lets the company add capacity only when demand is visible, which is why capex can be capped at INR 200–250 cr/yr while still growing 20%.
- **Scale in procurement:** "We are the largest purchaser of wire rods in the country today," and the company pays vendors in advance rather than stretching payables — deliberately trading working capital for buying power.
- **First-mover in Steel Cord:** "we are the first Indian company to get started" — a one-year approval cycle already sunk creates a real barrier for followers.
- **85-year customer relationships:** the decision to eat INR 5/kg rather than reprice committed orders was framed as the moat itself — "we are one of the very few companies who have taken this hit."
margins & cost dynamics: The business is cost-plus, with increases and decreases in raw material and consumables passed to the customer. The Q1 failure mode was speed, not structure: the cost jumped from a single day, while 30–40 days of orders were already priced. Management believes a sharp *fall* in prices could produce a symmetric one-time gain. Gas costs remain elevated (blended ~1.5x, up to 3x in some plants); the company leaned on alternative energy sources to restore production. Specialty carries structurally higher per-tonne margins; break-even for IHT/OHT is around 60% utilisation, with decent margins at 70–80%.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Capacity at the start of FY27 was 6.8 lakh tonnes with a further 60,000 T commissionable on demand — a deliberate policy of starting each year with 20–25% excess capacity. Historical operating sweet spot is 85–90% utilisation. Dadri greenfield had teething problems which are now resolved and ramping. OHT commissioning is the one dated milestone: end of FY27. The 2 lakh tonne Specialty ambition would need INR 2,000–2,500 cr of capex over four to five years and is explicitly gated on approvals and initial volumes.
capital allocation: Capex hard-capped at INR 200–250 cr/yr "to give us runway for each year", explicitly rejecting a lumpy high-capex year outside Specialty. Cash generation is being pulled from working capital: inventory days falling, receivables being renegotiated down, channel financing started with customers, and payable/vendor financing used — though management was pushed hard on this and conceded vendor financing substitutes one liability for another. It defended paying suppliers in advance as a pricing lever. Management flags a "structural change" in receivables over the next one to two years.
risks & watch-items:
- Gas cost has *not* normalised — margins are only restored because the cost was passed on. A demand slowdown would remove that pricing ability.
- Steel Cord has four trial stages left and no confirmed order; a 6–8 month timeline that has already taken a year to reach stage two.
- The 20% volume guidance implies ~145,000 T/quarter, i.e. ~85% utilisation — achievable historically but with no slack for another disruption.
- Vendor/payable financing flattering operating cash flow; the sustainable component is the receivable-days reduction, which is still promised rather than delivered.
- Asset turn on Specialty is ~1x (INR 2,000–2,500 cr capex for INR 2,000–2,500 cr peak revenue) — an analyst challenged whether Specialty adds any ROCE over the existing 16%. Management answered on absolute EBITDA (INR 600–800 cr) rather than rebutting the turn.
management quality / tone: Pranav Bansal was unusually specific and unhedged — he quantified the margin bridge to the rupee-per-kg and to the 45-day split rather than deflecting to "input cost pressure". He also volunteered the uncomfortable framing ("that strategy affected us badly"). Two moments of candour stand out: refusing to name the tyre customer, and correcting the CFO in real time on the Sanand land question ("Correction here. It is not that we are trying to sell off the entire facility"). On guidance he deliberately left himself room — "there could be Rs. 0.15 up or down… we would like to be a little comfortable here."
non-obvious takeaways:
- The cost-plus + natural-hedge design is normally invisible and only shows up when it fails; this quarter is the stress test, and it failed in exactly the way the design predicts (sudden, not gradual, move).
- B2C reached ~10% of sales inside a year off a doubling base — a faster consumer-channel build than the market is likely modelling, and it is margin-accretive, not dilutive.
- Management's growth algorithm is explicit and checkable: one third from existing customers growing, one third from market-share gain, one third from new products (250 new products/year, 20–25 new SKUs/month from R&D).
- The company started FY27 already holding the capacity needed to hit 20% growth — the guidance risk is demand, not supply.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Deck claims #1 largest stainless steel wire manufacturer in India (by volume) and #2 largest steel wire manufacturer in India (by volume), with ~7% market share in a 'fragmented but consolidating market'.
- Trust built over generations: 'nearly 9 decades of brand trust', with the journey slide dating the origin to 1938 as a trading steel wire house and incorporation in 1985; global footprint of ~40 countries supported.
- Diversified demand base: 5,000+ customers across sectors, 3,000+ SKUs, no single customer >~5% of revenue, no single sector >~25%, and ~90% retention among key/top customers, described as low concentration risk.
- Porter analysis frames entry barriers as brand equity, capacity of ~6.8 lakh MTPA (high capex barrier), scale economies from the largest single-location facility, 3,000+ SKUs and lead time to customers of under 48 hours.
- FY26 industry presence (annexure pie): Miscellaneous 23.1%, Automotive 21.9%, General Engineering 12.0%, Infrastructure 10.5%, Hardware 9.5%, Consumer Durables 9.4%, Cable 8.9%, Agriculture/Poultry 4.7%.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue/volume growth:** "we are still working towards achieving a growth of 20% for the rest of the year" — 20% volume growth; EBITDA guidance "would also still remain 20%", i.e. at least in line with volume.
- **Margin:** back to INR 7–8/kg blended EBITDA from ~15 May; specialty wires expected at a higher EBITDA than base business. IHT/OHT targeted at INR 10–20/kg once at optimum utilisation.
- **Order book / inflow:** no Steel Cord order book yet — trial stage only. Confirmed order book expected after 3–4 trial stages, each 2–3 months, i.e. 6–8 months out. More trial orders expected from other customers within Q2FY27.
- **Capex / commissioning:** INR 200–250 cr capex for FY27 and "every year" thereafter — deliberately capped. OHT to be commissioned by end of FY27, taking IHT+OHT capacity from 9,000 T to 15,000 T.
- **Returns:** 25% ROCE target in the *current* business "in a very short while", independent of Specialty.
- **Cash:** INR 350 cr operating cash flow target for FY27 (against INR 330 cr delivered in FY26 vs a INR 250 cr target); INR 800 cr combined across FY27+FY28.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Steel Cord import substitution:** 60–65% of the Indian market is served by imports; management targets 45–50% share at the 2 lakh tonne stage. Explicitly *not* an export play — Indian wire rod costs INR 10–15/kg more than Chinese, which is "50% of my margin".
- **IHT/OHT into EV:** both used in automotive, with EV a large part of consumption. 80% of IHT customers have already given approvals; the remaining 20% are at advanced stages. Targeting 50% IHT utilisation in the month following the call and 60–80% by end FY27.
- **B2C brand extension:** ambition is 50% of the low-carbon book through B2C, i.e. ~25% of total sales, at 20–30% higher EBITDA/tonne than B2B.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: The business is cost-plus, with increases and decreases in raw material and consumables passed to the customer. The Q1 failure mode was speed, not structure: the cost jumped from a single day, while 30–40 days of orders were already priced. Management believes a sharp *fall* in prices could produce a symmetric one-time gain. Gas costs remain elevated (blended ~1.5x, up to 3x in some plants); the company leaned on alternative energy sources to restore production. Specialty carries structurally higher per-tonne margins; break-even for IHT/OHT is around 60% utilisation, with decent margins at 70–80%.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Capex hard-capped at INR 200–250 cr/yr "to give us runway for each year", explicitly rejecting a lumpy high-capex year outside Specialty. Cash generation is being pulled from working capital: inventory days falling, receivables being renegotiated down, channel financing started with customers, and payable/vendor financing used — though management was pushed hard on this and conceded vendor financing substitutes one liability for another. It defended paying suppliers in advance as a pricing lever. Management flags a "structural change" in receivables over the next one to two years.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Pranav Bansal was unusually specific and unhedged — he quantified the margin bridge to the rupee-per-kg and to the 45-day split rather than deflecting to "input cost pressure". He also volunteered the uncomfortable framing ("that strategy affected us badly"). Two moments of candour stand out: refusing to name the tyre customer, and correcting the CFO in real time on the Sanand land question ("Correction here. It is not that we are trying to sell off the entire facility"). On guidance he deliberately left himself room — "there could be Rs. 0.15 up or down… we would like to be a little comfortable here."

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **Backward integration into machinery:** "more than 50% of our equipments we manufacture ourselves." This is the load-bearing advantage — it compresses capex planning from 12–18 months to six months and lets the company add capacity only when demand is visible, which is why capex can be capped at INR 200–250 cr/yr while still growing 20%.
- **Scale in procurement:** "We are the largest purchaser of wire rods in the country today," and the company pays vendors in advance rather than stretching payables — deliberately trading working capital for buying power.
- **First-mover in Steel Cord:** "we are the first Indian company to get started" — a one-year approval cycle already sunk creates a real barrier for followers.
- **85-year customer relationships:** the decision to eat INR 5/kg rather than reprice committed orders was framed as the moat itself — "we are one of the very few companies who have taken this hit."

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- Gas cost has *not* normalised — margins are only restored because the cost was passed on. A demand slowdown would remove that pricing ability.
- Steel Cord has four trial stages left and no confirmed order; a 6–8 month timeline that has already taken a year to reach stage two.
- The 20% volume guidance implies ~145,000 T/quarter, i.e. ~85% utilisation — achievable historically but with no slack for another disruption.
- Vendor/payable financing flattering operating cash flow; the sustainable component is the receivable-days reduction, which is still promised rather than delivered.
- Asset turn on Specialty is ~1x (INR 2,000–2,500 cr capex for INR 2,000–2,500 cr peak revenue) — an analyst challenged whether Specialty adds any ROCE over the existing 16%. Management answered on absolute EBITDA (INR 600–800 cr) rather than rebutting the turn.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The cost-plus + natural-hedge design is normally invisible and only shows up when it fails; this quarter is the stress test, and it failed in exactly the way the design predicts (sudden, not gradual, move).
- B2C reached ~10% of sales inside a year off a doubling base — a faster consumer-channel build than the market is likely modelling, and it is margin-accretive, not dilutive.
- Management's growth algorithm is explicit and checkable: one third from existing customers growing, one third from market-share gain, one third from new products (250 new products/year, 20–25 new SKUs/month from R&D).
- The company started FY27 already holding the capacity needed to hit 20% growth — the guidance risk is demand, not supply.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Gas/consumable shock compressed blended EBITDA to INR 4–4.5/kg (INR 2/kg for the first 45 days); revenue INR 1,168 cr +25% YoY on 112,000 MT. First Steel Cord bulk-trial order received. B2C at ~10% of sales. OCF INR 121 cr. 20% volume + 20% EBITDA growth guidance retained; capex capped at INR 200–250 cr; OHT commissioning promised by end FY27.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: did blended EBITDA/kg return to 7–8 for a full quarter; IHT utilisation vs the 50% target for August; further Steel Cord trial orders from other customers (promised "within this quarter"); volume run-rate vs the ~145,000 T/quarter implied by 20% growth; receivable days movement._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] The journey timeline records the acquisition of Bansal Steel & Power Limited in 2023.
- [IPO] Funds were raised through the IPO in 2024, alongside the launch of the Specialty Wire Segment and commencement of Dadri operations in January.
- [Macro] Geopolitical tensions in West Asia temporarily impacted demand and disrupted industrial gas supplies during the quarter; the MD states the company remains on track to deliver its growth targets of volumes and EBITDA for the remaining year as conditions normalise.
- [Shareholding] As on June 30, 2026: Promoter & Promoter Group 75.00%, DII 15.57%, Public 7.44%, FII 1.99%; outstanding shares 15,65,55,952 of face value 5.
- [Memberships] Member of the Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of India and of the Indian Stainless Steel Development Association.
